scope.focus: Electrical engineering with a power-engineering focus, from absolute electrical foundations through AC systems, machines, transformers, transmission, distribution, power flow, faults, protection, stability, control, power electronics, renewables, markets, planning, and modern-grid research literacy.
includes: Charge, current, voltage, energy, power, DC circuits, sinusoidal steady state, phasors, impedance, three-phase systems, and complex power
Magnetics, transformers, synchronous and induction machines, per-unit modeling, and single-line representations
Transmission, distribution, load modeling, power flow, faults, grounding, protection, voltage control, frequency control, and stability
Power electronics, HVDC, FACTS, renewable generation, battery storage, inverter-based resources, DERs, and microgrids
State estimation, SCADA/EMS, reliability, resilience, markets, optimization, planning, simulation, interconnection standards, and cybersecurity
Computational reproduction, systems design, critical paper reading, research-question formation, and frontier refreshes
delegates: General mathematical machinery may import explicit prerequisites from Linear Algebra or Complex Analysis when advanced derivations require it rather than silently assuming those skills.
Low-level programming and large software projects may import explicit prerequisites from C++ or Computer Systems when computational projects require them.
